kind: A full-size pilot of 24,000 updates, one seed: the looped stack with a third pass of its middle levels.
why: Depth by recurrence is the one part that adds knowledge to the full-size stack at equal parameters: levels 2 to 8 run twice are 0.0096 ahead of the plain stack at its best rate and 0.019 ahead of the same pulses without the loop after 24,000 updates (full_size_loop_pilot.json). On the test bed the loop holds with data, and there its middle levels run three times: level 0 once, levels 1 to 4 three times, level 5 once, 0.025 and 0.017 ahead of the bed with the same pulses after 6,000 and 24,000 updates and 0.020 and 0.025 ahead of the plain bed on two more seeds (loop_with_data.json). At full size only two passes were tried. More passes are more computation on the same synapses, as cortex iterates over what it hears; the stack's distance to the Transformer is 0.034 at each model's best rate (full_size_best_rate_pair.json), and the loop is the part most likely to close a large share of it. A third pass costs pulses: Daniel allowed more pulses if that is what wins, as an arm of its own with its cost stated.

arms.fs-loop9: --stack-loop 2,8,3 --pulse-budget 705000: levels 2 to 8 run three times, 25 level passes on the synapses of 11, the budget of 310,000 scaled by 25/11 and rounded to the nearest thousand; 34,810,900 parameters, as the plain stack

base: fs-loop6 of full_size_loop_pilot (1.31024): levels 2 to 8 run twice, budget 507,000, the same recipe, code copy and seed. Beside it fs-st6 (1.31985, the plain stack at 310,000) and fs-b507 (1.32913, the plain stack at 507,000: more pulses alone are 0.0093 worse).
runs: sched/bin/full.sh stack fs-loop9 --lr 6e-4 --stack-loop 2,8,3 --pulse-budget 705000 on the code copy that trained fs-loop6 (v17n): v16's stack with forgetting slopes and the pool of fine quanta, windows of 512 bytes, batch 8, 24,000 updates, warmup 1,000, cosine over the run, seed 20001; on GPU 1 after the loop's full-length run (fsp-loop) and the full-size unit diagnostic's first two arms.
measure: As every full-size pilot: averaged weights on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 lead bytes, bits of every piece kept; paired with fs-loop6 and with fs-st6 (experiments/compare_stream_scores.py), split by context (experiments/gap_by_piece.py, near 496, far 8,192). Beside the bits: the trainer's pulses a byte, the training time and the peak GPU memory.
reading: One seed: this reading picks a recipe and is not a finding about recurrence. The third pass adds knowledge if fs-loop9 is at least 0.005 better than fs-loop6 with the paired interval clear of zero; the loop's next full-length run then takes three passes, at 2.27 times the plain stack's pulses and about twice its training time, which every report of it states. Within 0.003 of fs-loop6 the third pass adds nothing and two passes stay. Between, unclear, reported only. Because more pulses alone hurt the plain stack (fs-b507), a gain here is read as the third pass's and not the budget's; the gain on new contexts is reported beside it. If the loop's full-length run (full_size_loop_run.json) finds that the loop's gain fades with data, this pilot is reported and builds nothing.
seen_before_recording: full_size_loop_pilot.json, full_size_loop_run.json and full_size_loop_variants.json as recorded (the full-length run is half done and unscored; the variants have not trained); loop_with_data.json with its result; the pilot's memory: fs-loop6 trained in half of a GPU's memory beside another run. No run of this record has started.
